keyframe_review.note: 28,456 km2 for 1856-1884 (92 cells: Zanzibar, Pemba, Mafia and the coast from the Rufiji to about Tanga, with the Mombasa mainland). The row's label and Wikipedia title are those of the 1964 republic (People's Republic of Zanzibar page: 'founded in 1964'); the shape is the sultanate. The Sultanate of Zanzibar page says only that 'Until 1884, the Sultans of Zanzibar controlled a substantial portion of the Swahili Coast', and the Omani Empire page that the African dominion ran to 12 miles south of the Ruvuma River; the division of 1856 gave Majid that whole dominion, which Cliopatria drew as 64,591 km2 in 1837-1839 (ratio 0.44, beyond a factor of two). So the shape is too small: it omits Kilwa and the coast south of the Rufiji, and the Kenyan coast north of Mombasa. No page gives an infobox area. The Banadir coast is a vassal in the ledger.

correction.text: the strip of 1856 with Siyu added in 1863; the ledger's 1887 and 1888 losses are taken off it

keyframe_review.note: 28,456 km2 for 1885-1889, identical to 1856-1884. The German East Africa page says that 'In November 1886 Germany and Britain reached an agreement' respecting 'the Sultan of Zanzibar's islands and the coastal strip', so the strip survives as the base shape; the ledger then removes Mombasa (25 May 1887) and the mainland coast leased to the German company (28 April 1888). Siyu, submitted in 1863, is added.

region.text: the Cape Delgado-Lamu strip with Zanzibar, Pemba, Mafia and Mombasa that the Omani Empire page calls the African dominion

ledger.note: 19 October 1856: Majid bin Said becomes the first Sultan of Zanzibar. 'After his death in 1856, two of his sons, Majid bin Said and Thuwaini bin Said, struggled over the succession'; 'Majid became the first Sultan of Zanzibar, but obliged to pay an annual tribute to the Omani court in Muscat'; infobox 'Divided dynasty: 19 October 1856'.

1856: the Banadir coast is allotted to Zanzibar. 'Jurisdiction over the Banadir coast was allotted to the Sultan of Zanzibar because of instability in Muscat'; the claim stayed nominal (a fort at Kismayo in 1869, a governor of Mogadishu 1872-1893 on the same page).

region.text: Siyu, on the north coast of Pate Island (approximate position; the gazetteer lacks Siyu)

ledger.note: 1863: Siyu submits to Zanzibar. 'When Siyu finally succumbed to Zanzibar's dominance, under Sultan Majid in 1863', one of the last towns on the Swahili coast to do so, after beating Said's army in 1845. The page does not say whether Pate town submitted with it.

25 May 1887: Mombasa is relinquished to the British East Africa Association. 'On 25 May 1887 Mombasa was relinquished to the British East Africa Association, later the Imperial British East Africa Company'; the Sultanate of Zanzibar page has the company taking over the administration of Mombasa from 1888.

region.text: the Sultan's mainland coast within what became German East Africa (Cliopatria's 1888 shape cut by the Tanganyika mainland; the pages give no line)

ledger.note: 28 April 1888: Sultan Khalifah bin Said signs the coast over to the German East Africa Company. 'On 28 April 1888, Sultan Khalifah bin Said finally signed a treaty'; the page speaks of a lease and says that 'From August 1888, the company tried to take over the coastal towns', which set off the Abushiri revolt. The German government assumed control on 1 January 1891.

region.text: Zanzibar, the islands of Unguja and Pemba

ledger.note: 1 July 1890: Zanzibar becomes a British protectorate. The Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty was 'signed on 1 July 1890' and Britain 'immediately declared a protectorate over Zanzibar'; the Sultanate of Zanzibar page adds that with the treaty 'Zanzibar itself became a British protectorate'. The sultan stayed on the throne; the map passes the islands to Britain as a protectorate tint.

wars.name: Abushiri revolt

zones.text: the Sultan's mainland coast within what became German East Africa (Cliopatria's 1888 shape cut by the Tanganyika mainland; the pages give no line)

wars.outcome: German East Africa Company administration of the coast set off a revolt in 1888; Abushiri was 'captured and executed on 15 December 1889' and the German government took control on 1 January 1891.
wars.note: 'The German and British navies collaborated in establishing a blockade of the East African coast.' The page does not say what part the Sultan's own forces played, and the Zanzibar-held coast was already leased.

certainty.note: No line is given by the pages: the Sultan's dominion is a coastal strip and its claims ('Until 1884 ... a substantial portion of the Swahili Coast'). The November 1886 Anglo-German agreement respected 'the Sultan of Zanzibar's islands and the coastal strip' but the pages do not give its width.

notes:
Cliopatria's row 'People's Republic of Zanzibar' (1856-1889) is the Sultanate of Zanzibar: the Wikipedia title and Wikidata id Q157535 it carries belong to the 1964 republic (infobox 'Zanzibar Revolution: 12 January 1964', merger with Tanganyika 26 April; 'founded in 1964'). The dossier keeps the Cliopatria slug and Wikipedia field as the schema requires and names the state for what it was. A separate row, sultanate-of-zanzibar (1963-1966, Q157904), is the last years of the same sultanate; whoever owns it should link it to this one (it is outside this batch). Colours: the registry gave the two rows different colours.

Life span: Cliopatria ends the row in 1889; the sultanate went on as a British protectorate until 10 December 1963 (Sultanate of Zanzibar page) and the dossier ends it as a sovereign state on 1 July 1890 (Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty). Someone should decide whether the protectorate years are drawn as the vassal tint of British Colonial Empire or as a continuation of this dossier; this one ends where Cliopatria's shape plus the pages leave it.

Shape: the 28,456 km2 shape is too small for the dominion described (see the keyframe notes); the corrected base is the Omani coast strip of 1837-1839. Kilwa and the south, Lamu and the north: no page opened dates Zanzibari rule there, so the strip is kept whole, unverified.

Left out (not on the pages opened): Majid's reign beyond the infobox 1856-1870, the later sultans (Barghash, Khalifah named only in passing), the 1861 Canning award, Italian leases of the Banadir, Witu, the 1895 East Africa Protectorate, the 1896 Anglo-Zanzibar War (outside the life span), the German purchase of the strip in 1890 (the Abushiri page speaks of a lease and has no 1890 purchase). The German strip is Cliopatria's 1888 shape cut by the Tanganyika mainland region, so Mafia Island falls on the German side without a page saying so.

Page budget: 1-2 pages were allowed; six pages were used because the 1885-1890 events (Mombasa 1887, the 1888 lease, the 1890 treaty) are only on the Mombasa, Abushiri, German East Africa and Heligoland-Zanzibar pages, which the German and British gains of the 1890s need anyway.

Counterparts needing dossiers: german-africa (Cliopatria's 'German Africa' row, af-08; it draws German Tanzania only from 1895, so the 1888 coastal lease and the 1 January 1891 takeover have no shape there), imperial-british-east-africa-company (1887/1888-1895, the Kenya coast; af-08), british-colonial-empire (eu-11, for the 1890 protectorate), pate-sultanate (this batch). Gazetteer names needed: Pate, Siyu, Faza, Mafia Island.
